method: Every source and target string read, and first-path canonical context resolved for all220. Canonical context itself is English-authored Korean-teaching material; no separate Korean-language canonical was invented. Korean text/romanization/ending examples and meaning/instruction roles were compared. Automated surface checks complement this reading, not replace it.
independence: Reviewer did not author PCM Korean course. AI review only; not native-speaker or teacher approval.
semanticAssessment: No additional material target meaning change identified across220. Shared Pidgin words such as milk/tree/person/family and technical labels are valid overlaps and not automatically untranslated. Some choices require regional/naturalness review.

specificChecks.Ksteps: 99,102,105,108,111,114,117,120,123,126 say Korean course step1..10. No claim that these equal the official six TOPIK levels is added. K7/K8/K9/K10 review labels remain course-stage labels.
specificChecks.gender: 203/204 explicitly preserve source female-speaker usage of 오빠/언니; this is source-explicit grammatical-cultural teaching, not inference from a name. No unsupported named-person gender setting added.
specificChecks.learningTargets: All Hangul/jamo runs, digit tokens, blank runs and placeholders matched exactly in surface checks; romanized examples were also read. Korean target morphology is preserved.
specificChecks.meanings: Mixed examples keep Korean and romanization while explaining meanings with Pidgin/shared vocabulary; metadata exceptions listed below.
specificChecks.150: Pronunciation analogy is a source teaching limitation, not a PCM translation error.

sourceGuidanceLimitations.reason: English skate starts with /s/, so first sound in skate is not a valid model for all five tense consonants. Tight-throat instruction is also an oversimplified phonetic guide. Target faithfully follows source; phonetics teacher/audio review needed.
Between r and l is a beginner approximation of Korean ㄹ, not an exact articulatory account.

hakgyo is orthographic romanization while actual school pronunciation has tensed second consonant; source mixes romanization with pronunciation guidance. Target retains hakgyo and explicitly mentions tensing, consistent with source.
Polite forms are broadly summarized as -요/-니다; actual Korean ending morphology/register requires context.
Adding 요 is a simplified politeness rule, not a universal transformation.
Native versus Sino-Korean number uses depend on classifier/context; source provides beginner examples rather than exhaustive distribution.
Consonant-to-vowel linking explanation is broad; batchim sound changes and word-boundary conditions require teacher/audio confirmation.

limitations: No audio or rendered lesson testing.
No target files modified; proposals only.
